quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Only at night.
Only during the day.
Both day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing anytime you ride to stay visible.

questions.question: What should you do about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: Don't worry about them.
Check them regularly.
They don't exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes. Make this a regular habit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during the day, you should:

options.text: Not wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright clothing when riding to make yourself more noticeable, even during the day.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medicine before riding?

options.text: It's usually safe because over-the-counter drugs are not very strong.
It's always acceptable.
It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view.
They show a wider view.
They show a better view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, vehicles in convex mirrors may look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointed downward with your toes.
Relaxed and hanging down.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Don't point your toes downward, as they could get caught between the road and footrests.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly to your commands when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves to prevent skidding.
Ride on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake doesn't work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves to prevent skidding.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes in speed or direction cause skids. Be smooth when speeding up, shifting gears, turning, or braking.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other motorists?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors when riding.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Before riding a motorcycle, you should check the throttle. What should it do?

options.text: Stay in place when you release it.
Stay loose when you release it.
Spring back quickly when you release it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spring back quickly when you release it.
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should spring back quickly when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Drive through with caution.
Turn around and find a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely and wait until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface ahead
Other traffic around you
Conditions that stay the same as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that stay the same as you approach
questions.explanation: Look for potential problems on the road. Plan ahead to reduce their risks.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for the weather.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road while avoiding another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-motorcycle crashes is turning too wide in a curve or turn. This can make a motorcycle leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until it starts moving again.
Change to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside help vehicle with flashing lights, move to a different lane and give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the most danger of conflicts with other vehicles.

options.text: On the highway
Near an intersection
In a group

questions.correctAnswerText: Near an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles are most likely to conflict. Position yourself where other drivers can see you.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they actually are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Other drivers may misjudge your speed and location.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how far back should a motorcycle rider stay from the vehicle ahead?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use a larger distance in poor weather or difficult conditions.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle in the rain, where should you ride?

options.text: Down the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get the best grip.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, should you move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther away from the passing vehicle.
No, because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
It does not matter, as it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: What should you wear to make other drivers see you better?

options.text: Brightly-colored clothing.
Dark-colored clothing.
Wave your arms while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you at any time of day.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol you drink
Your body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: Your BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not play a major role.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Help you see others and help others see you.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Allow other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and help others see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and help them see you. It should keep you away from other drivers' blind spots and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what must you do with tire pressure?

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.
